title: Cuckoos host range is associated positively with distribution range and negatively with evolutionary uniqueness

original_source.central_claim: positive host-richness versus breeding-range and negative host-richness versus evolutionary-distinctiveness associations among brood-parasitic cuckoos

central_claims: Among brood-parasitic cuckoos, more host species are associated with a larger breeding distribution.
Controlling breeding range and phylogeny, more host species are associated with lower cuckoo evolutionary distinctiveness.
Evolutionary distinctiveness does not significantly differ between parasitic and non-parasitic cuckoos.

source_manifest.title: Cuckoos host range is associated positively with distribution range and negatively with evolutionary uniqueness
source_manifest.finding: Across cuckoos, host richness rises with breeding range and falls with evolutionary distinctiveness; the paper cautions that host counts imperfectly measure selectivity.

source_manifest.title: Diet specialization and brood parasitism in cuckoo species
source_manifest.finding: Morelli, Benedetti and Møller revisit related diet specialization and discuss their earlier host-range findings; the team overlaps the original.

source_manifest.title: Biodiversity indicators for breeding passerines in a multiple-cuckoo system in China: A comparison of cuckoos and raptors
source_manifest.finding: Lin and Liang compare bioindicators across China and invoke passive host sampling in discussion. Liang coauthored the original; this is a different ecological outcome.

answers.rationale: The located diet and bioindicator studies share original authors and do not independently retest the joint cuckoo host-richness, range and ED association.
No independent rerun using the deposited 42-species analysis or newly collected cuckoo host-richness data was located.
The China bioindicator comparison measures passerine diversity; it is not a larger test of cuckoo host richness versus cuckoo ED.
The original authors restate their finding in 2020; a later independent authoritative assessment of the joint association was not verified.
No located follow-up replaces raw host counts with parasitism rates or explicitly controls uneven research effort to test the stated limitation.
The two most direct follow-ups share original authors; neither establishes an independent extension of the specified analysis.
Two publications were located, but author overlap and differing outcomes prevent counting them as two independent groups building on this result.
The sources discuss prior findings, but no independent reuse of this paper’s particular dataset or fitted model was verified. PGLS itself predates the paper.
Brood-parasitism reviews were located, but none read explicitly credits this particular ED association with enabling a new direction.
Comparisons of cuckoos and raptors are not comparisons against the original host-range model; no qualifying independent baseline use was verified.
The original suggests conservation relevance; later discussion does not demonstrate an independent conservation or scientific benefit from applying this specific association.
The China study concerns biodiversity surrogacy and shares an author; successful transfer of the original association to honeyguides, cowbirds or other parasites remains unverified.
The diet and bioindicator results are related, but neither source read establishes that the 2018 joint association enabled its result.
No conservation prioritization plan or monitoring workflow explicitly applying this model was found; archive availability does not establish deployment.
This comparative natural-history study proposes an association, not a performance advantage over an alternative method.
The 2025 paper invokes passive sampling in interpretation, but does not demonstrably apply the original cuckoo-level model or data. Substantive late reuse is unresolved.
The 2025 discussion shares an author and refers to a different host-level outcome; an independent positive assessment of the central result is unverified.
Related papers in 2020 and 2025 share authors; the required independent substantive follow-up in two years was not established.
No independent synthesis adopting this particular cuckoo ED result as valid or useful was verified.
Later citations do not compare the result with updated phylogenies, better host-selectivity measures or other alternatives; continued usefulness remains unresolved.

search_gaps: Publisher opens were intermittent; the complete original author manuscript was downloaded and read. Follow-up indexed abstract/discussion scopes are explicit.
The 2025 study discusses host-species ED, whereas the target evaluates cuckoo-species ED; these outcomes are not interchangeable.
Searches covered exact identity, the ED/host-richness claim, criticism, later conservation studies and author overlap. No independent direct retest was verified.
Lifetime observation through 2026-09-16; the assigned pilot sample is not an unbiased estimate of all research outcomes.
research.summary: The full original establishes a clear comparative claim and acknowledges host-count limitations. Located later studies overlap the authors and do not establish independent validation or operational conservation use; missing outcomes remain unknown.
